model_annotations.Bulgarian: This plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPPA output as a function of layer. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” ranges from 0 to 20, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 1, representing discrete layers. The y-axis, which displays “Sparsity Ratio,” is a linear scale, starting at approximately 0 and extending to a maximum value of 1.0. A dashed blue line represents the sparsity ratio before a gate, with an average value of 0.03 at layer 0 and decreasing to approximately 0.08 at layer 20. A dotted orange line represents the sparsity ratio after a gate, with an average value of 0.44 at layer 0 and decreasing to approximately 0.38 at layer 20. Finally, a green line represents the sparsity ratio after average gate, with an average value of 0.33 at layer 0 and decreasing to approximately 0.15 at layer 20.
